cues.text:
Let’s put the earlier lessons together.
A workflow tells us what happens next
and when we should stop.

Begin with the issue and plan, then
prove the bug with a failing test.

Apply the fix, run the suite, and hand
off the pull request.

At each point, name the person who
checks the evidence before the next step
goes ahead.

Start in Plan and supply the issue,
source, and tests.

The proposal should add one assertion
and change one comparison while keeping
the public signature.

The author reads the plan against the
issue. If a new dependency or signature

change appears, send the plan back for
revision.

Begin editing once the proposed scope
fits the requirement.

Add the regression test and run it in
the approved environment.

The useful failure names zero and shows
that the validator returned true.

If the test command never ran, or an
import failed,
return to the setup and repeat it.

The author should be able to point to
evidence that this assertion detects
this defect on the original revision.

After the fix, rerun the same tests. If
the zero case still fails or an existing

case breaks, pause and inspect the
change.

If all four pass, check the remaining
diff and save the run output.

This checkpoint uses the result of the
actual suite.

A plausible summary from the agent can
explain the change while the test output
provides the evidence.

Use the skill from the previous lesson
to organize the handover.

Give it the issue, the patch, and the
test output you verified.

Read its draft and correct any
unsupported claim.

The author then opens the pull request
through the approved workflow.

In the training repository, the
configured CI checks provide additional

evidence about the revision the peer
will see.

Now hand the pull request number to a
teammate.

They use their authorized terminal
account to read the PR,

inspect the patch, and check the
required results.

They decide whether to approve or ask
for a correction.

Their review and the configured merge
rules are part of the workflow.

The author's agent can assist with the
draft,

while the peer records their own
decision.

Try the workflow twice with a teammate.
Once,

run it with the complete evidence and
record the review outcome.

Again, remove the regression output or
simulate a failing required check.

Say where work stops and what would let
it resume.

The rehearsal is successful when both of
you can name the owner, evidence,
and next action for either outcome.
